extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, researchers and anyone submitting or cataloging solutions journalism stories to the Solutions Story Tracker
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for submitting, vetting, tagging, and including solutions journalism stories in the Solutions Story Tracker — including the four core qualities of solutions journalism, basic submission requirements, metadata/taxonomy and vetting process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describes a response to a problem and how it works
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes a response to a problem and how it works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed as one of the four qualities of solutions journalism used by Story Tracker vetters to evaluate submissions. The story should focus on a concrete response (program, policy, practice, innovation) and explain operational details of how it functions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seeks to draw out insights that explain success or failure
rubrics_metrics.description: Seeks to draw out insights that explain success or failure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should go beyond descriptive reporting to identify and analyze the factors that contributed to the response’s outcomes (what worked, what didn’t). This is one of the four mandatory evaluation qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presents the available evidence about the effectiveness of a response
rubrics_metrics.description: Presents the available evidence about the effectiveness of a response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should include the evidence (data, evaluations, credible measurements) about whether the response achieved its goals. Vetters evaluate how well the story presents and contextualizes that evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explains the shortcomings or limitations of the response
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the shortcomings or limitations of the response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A solutions story must acknowledge limits, unintended consequences, scalability constraints, or areas where the response fell short — this is explicitly one of the four evaluation qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic submission requirements (news outlet, date, byline)
rubrics_metrics.description: The story must come from a news outlet and have a date and a byline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are baseline inclusion checks performed by the Story Tracker team. Submissions that lack a verifiable outlet, date, or byline may be rejected; registrants are asked to sign in so they can track submission status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source credibility (news outlet editorial infrastructure)
rubrics_metrics.description: Solutions Story Tracker ensures each story comes from a credible news source that has its own editorial infrastructure; SJN does not fact-check stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The team verifies outlet credibility (editorial infrastructure) rather than performing independent fact-checking. Inclusion in the Tracker does not imply endorsement of the initiatives, policies, organizations or approaches featured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting process and AI-assisted review
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted stories are sent to a Solutions Story Tracker team member who evaluates the story for the four qualities and the basic checks; an AI tool is used to assist but does not replace human judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI is used to manage volume and support evaluation, but final decisions and tagging are made by human vetters. If a story falls short, the team will include the reason for exclusion when communicating with the submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required metadata and tagging (issue area, date, language, location, institution, SDG, outlet, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories are tagged with structured metadata such as issue area, language, date, news outlet and location, institution leading the response, Sustainable Development Goal, tribal land, and other contextual fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate tagging improves discoverability and supports filters/collections. The site provides exhaustive controlled lists (issue areas, success factors, outlets, locations, tribal lands) for consistent categorization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Success Factors taxonomy for categorization
rubrics_metrics.description: A defined set of 'Success Factors' identify ways community members overcome big challenges (examples: Using Creative Financing; Expanding Access; Impact measurement; Building trust; Collective action; Meeting people where they are at).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitters should select relevant success factors when tagging stories. Success Factors are used as filters and analytical lenses to surface insights and trends; the site links to a 'Learn more' page about how success factors are defined and used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media type and length classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories must be classified by media type (e.g., Text, Podcast, Video, Photojournalism, Multi-media, Broadcast TV) and length (e.g., Under 800 Words; 800–1500 Words; 1500–3000 Words; Over 3000 Words; Under 3 Minutes; 3–5 Minutes; 5–15 Minutes; Over 15 Minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selecting correct media type and length is part of submission/tagging and supports search and filtering in the Tracker.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for visual equity
rubrics_metrics.description: The site follows an external guide for using equitable visuals when choosing images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SJN worked with the Authority Collective to develop a guide for equitable visuals and follows that guide in selecting images for the website; submitters and curators should be aware of visual equity considerations when presenting stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common reasons for exclusion / 'miss the mark' criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tracker documents common reasons why a story may miss the mark for inclusion (linked from the page).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a submission falls short, the vetting team provides the reason. Submitters are encouraged to consult the 'common reasons why a story may miss the mark' guidance to improve future submissions.
